- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +1.5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak (e.g., > +0.3), model often underreacts; increase forecast slope gently to reflect sentiment shift.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–5 days ahead); add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast values for short-term bias.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–+0.3), model often overestimates upside; cap forecast growth at 1.0–1.5% above recent mean.  
- Model frequently fails to capture mean reversion in 10–15 day horizon; if sentiment is neutral, add a slight downward drift (–0.1 to –0.3) to mid-term forecast.
